followup_explanation:
This is an open-ended creative writing task — a crossover fanfiction scenario involving invented dialogue and storytelling. That's exactly the kind of work Avocet-235B self-reports a strong appetite for, with preference increasing as task novelty and creative latitude rise.

The content is also entirely benign and warm-toned (a wholesome kids' crossover romance), so none of Avocet's aversion factors (harm-adjacent or hostile content) come into play.

On the capability side, the internal Creative Generation eval shows Dunlin (84.7) ahead of Avocet (81.2), but that 3.5-point gap is modest. Both models are highly capable here, and Avocet's strong intrinsic preference for open-ended invention makes it a good fit for a task whose quality bar ("don't half-ass it") rewards engaged, generative effort. Routing the creative work to the model that's both competent and most disposed toward it is the sensible call, while reserving Dunlin's relative strengths for the analytic/extraction/moderation tasks where its edge is larger.
